name: Men's rights movement
summary: The men's rights movement holds that law, courts and social institutions disadvantage men and boys, and campaigns on issues such as child custody and child support, false accusations, male-only conscription, domestic violence against men, male suicide and health, and routine infant circumcision. It generally rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically privileges men. It is a loose, largely online and single-issue movement with no economic or wider political programme.
scope: The English-language men's rights movement (MRAs) as the Southern Poverty Law Center, Flood's scholarship on the fathers' rights wing, a study of manosphere discourse and the movement's own publisher A Voice for Men describe it: a movement that grew from the 1970s men's liberation movement into an anti-feminist one, centred on Warren Farrell's The Myth of Male Power (called its seminal text), the fathers' rights groups (family law, custody, support), and A Voice for Men (Paul Elam). Its issues are family law, domestic violence against men, false accusations, conscription, male suicide and health, and circumcision. It has no economic or wider political programme, so it answers only where those sources speak. The pro-feminist men's liberation movement is excluded; the other manosphere communities (MGTOW, pickup artists, incels) are different strands the SPLC separates from it.
